newsitem.title: USA: Invacare says Healthdyne offer expires.
newsitem.headline: Invacare says Healthdyne offer expires.

text.p: Invacare Corp. Friday said its $200 million hostile tender offer to acquire medical device company Healthdyne Technologies Inc. has expired without any shares being purchased.
Invacare, a medical equipment company which had launched the $15-a-share cash bid for Healthdyne, said the depositary will return all shares tendered in the offer and not withdrawn.

The announcement marked a victory for Healthdyne, whose management has engaged in a six-month fight for control of the Marietta, Ga.-based company. On Wednesday, shareholders re-elected Healthdyne's slate of directors, rejecting a dissident slate offered by Elyria, Ohio-based Invacare.

Invacare Chairman and Chief Executive Malachi Mixon said in a statement that based on the proxies the company had received, it appeared that Healthdyne's board was elected, and "there is no point in continuing our tender offer at this time."
"We continue to be interested in acquiring Healthdyne, but we cannot wait around idly," he added.
